rule: Do not use `caplog` in provider tests; use direct log capture or logical assertions instead
trigger: caplog` appears in a test function in providers/**/*.py
rationale: caplog has been banned because it produces negative side effects when tests adjust log levels or run in parallel; the reviewer explicitly states it was banned some time ago

evidence.excerpt: Since some time be banned caplog for testing — generated negative side effects

rule: Avoid real `asyncio.sleep` calls in trigger unit tests; patch `asyncio.sleep` or use `asyncio.wait_for` to assert non-completion
trigger: asyncio.sleep` with a literal float/int appears inside a test function in providers/**/triggers/test_*.py
rationale: Real sleeps add wall-clock time to the CI suite and can be flaky on slow runners; the reviewer recommends patching sleep or using wait_for with a small timeout to verify the trigger does not yield immediately

evidence.excerpt: adds noticeable wall-clock time to unit suite and can be flaky on slow CI

rule: When adding a new operator entry to the operators `index.rst` table, also bump the operator count stated in the prose above the table and add a matching descriptive paragraph
trigger: A new `* -` row is added to the operators comparison table in `providers/**/docs/operators/index.rst` without updating the operator count sentence
rationale: The file explicitly states how many operators the provider ships; adding an entry without updating the count leaves the count stale; the reviewer also requires a descriptive paragraph per operator consistent with existing ones

evidence.excerpt: line 24 still says 'five operators' — this PR makes it six, bump the count

rule: In `AIRFLOW_CONN_*` quickstart doc examples, encode `extra` as a nested JSON object, not as a JSON-serialised string
trigger: `extra` value in an `AIRFLOW_CONN_` shell export is a quoted JSON string (e.g. `'\"model\": ...'`) rather than a plain nested object
rationale: `Connection.from_json` accepts a nested object for `extra`; the string form is error-prone and the reviewer verified the nested form resolves the model end-to-end

evidence.excerpt: nested-JSON-as-a-string extra is the error-prone form; nested object equally valid

rule: Keep `provider.yaml` field descriptions consistent with the current schema; remove references to parameters that have been deleted
trigger: A `description:` value in `provider.yaml` references a field name that no longer exists in the same connection type block
rationale: Stale cross-references in provider.yaml mislead users configuring connections; the reviewer flagged the same stale text appearing in both provider.yaml and the auto-generated get_provider_info.py

evidence.excerpt: removed `service_account_file` a few rounds ago, so this reference is stale

rule: Example DAGs must be self-contained and copy-pasteable; do not extract shared helpers across example DAG files
trigger: A function or class defined outside an example DAG file is imported and used inside `providers/**/example_dags/*.py`
rationale: Example DAGs are meant to serve as starting points; extracting helpers makes them harder to use independently; intentional duplication is acceptable

evidence.excerpt: Example DAGs should be self-contained and copy-pasteable; duplication is intentional

rule: Example DAGs must not wrap optional-dependency imports in `try/except`; import errors should surface immediately
trigger: A `try: import ...; except ImportError` block appears inside `providers/**/example_dags/*.py`
rationale: Example DAGs should fail clearly when a dependency is missing rather than silently hiding functionality; the try/except guard was intentionally removed in this provider

evidence.excerpt: example DAGs should fail clearly on missing deps rather than silently hiding functionality

rule: Do not manually edit `get_provider_info.py`; all changes must go to `provider.yaml` and be regenerated via `prek run update-providers-build-files`
trigger: A diff modifies `providers/**/get_provider_info.py` directly without a corresponding change to the same provider's `provider.yaml`
rationale: get_provider_info.py is auto-generated; manual edits will be overwritten the next time the build-file update tool is run

evidence.excerpt: auto-generated from provider.yaml — manual edits will be overwritten by prek run

rule: When a hook subclass ignores parent-signature parameters (e.g. `api_key`, `base_url`) in favour of `extra`, document this explicitly in the docstring
trigger: A method in `providers/**/hooks/*.py` has parameters with the same names as `extra` keys but reads from `extra` rather than the parameters without a docstring note
rationale: Having the same field name in two sources (method param vs. extra) is confusing; the reviewer requires either renaming extra keys or a docstring note that the parent params are intentionally unused

evidence.excerpt: having the same field name in two sources is confusing; add a note or rename

rule: When hook/operator docs claim a parameter overrides a spec-file value, the implementation must only pass that parameter conditionally (omit it when unset) so the spec file's value is used as a fallback
trigger: A hook method unconditionally passes a keyword argument to an underlying factory (e.g. `Agent.from_file(model=self.get_conn(), ...)`) when docs state the spec file supplies the default
rationale: Unconditionally passing the argument overrides the spec file regardless of whether the user set a connection model, contradicting documented behaviour and raising errors when neither source is configured

evidence.excerpt: unconditionally overrides whatever model: is declared in the spec file

rule: When a parameter appends to rather than replaces spec-file content, docs, docstrings, test names, and example names must say 'appended'/'merged', not 'overrides'
trigger: A docstring or RST file uses the word 'overrides' for a parameter that the underlying library (pydantic-ai, etc.) merges/appends with the spec-file value
rationale: pydantic-ai's `from_spec` concatenates instructions rather than replacing them; claiming override semantics misleads users and the test only asserts kwarg forwarding to a mock, missing the merge behaviour

evidence.excerpt: three spots claim override: the RST, the :param docstring, and the example name

rule: When an operator parameter replaces a built-in default prompt rather than appending to it, the docstring must say 'overrides' not 'appended to'
trigger: An operator docstring says a `system_prompt` or similar param is 'appended to' or 'additional instructions' but the implementation assigns it directly (replacing the default)
rationale: Users need accurate semantics to know whether they must manually concatenate the default; the reviewer notes the current docstring implies additive behaviour while the code replaces the default entirely

evidence.excerpt: docstring says 'Additional instructions appended' but system_prompt overrides the default

rule: Plugin FastAPI sub-apps mounted under the Airflow webserver must add per-route or router-level `Depends(requires_access_*)` auth dependencies; do not rely on parent-app middleware alone
trigger: A FastAPI app or router is defined in `providers/**/plugins/*.py` and its route handlers lack `Depends(requires_access_*)` or equivalent auth dependency
rationale: Plugin sub-apps mounted via `app.mount()` do not inherit route-level auth from the parent; JWTRefreshMiddleware only refreshes tokens and does not reject unauthenticated requests; without explicit auth any user with network access can call the endpoints

evidence.excerpt: anyone with network access to the webserver can approve, reject, or submit feedback
